stories.event: The Fed's FOMC ends its 27–28 Oct meeting with a rate decision at 14:00 EDT (19:00 CET) on 28 Oct, Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference ~14:30 EDT. The range is 3.75–4.00% after a 12–0 25 bp hike in September (first since 2023); no projections at this meeting. In July three regional presidents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) dissented for a hike; June and September were unanimous. Economists expect a hold (Newsquawk: 94/100 in the Reuters poll); September projections pointed to a possible December hike.

stories.event: Chancellor John Healey (government of PM Andy Burnham) delivers his first Budget on Wed 28 Oct 2026, statement after PMQs at about 12:30 GMT (13:30 CET); OBR Economic and Fiscal Outlook and Treasury documents follow on gov.uk. Pre-briefed: a bank tax rise (reversing the 2023 cut of the bank surcharge from 8% to 3%, about GBP 2bn a year; levy or windfall options), a decision on the 5p fuel duty cut that expires 31 Dec 2026 (default: 52.95p -> 55.95p in January 2027, 57.95p in March), protection of low-income pensioners from income tax. Fiscal hole about GBP 12bn tied to the Middle East war; headroom expected well below March's GBP 23.6bn.

claims.label: Constitutional Court rules on interim measure
claims.text: By 23:59 Prague time on 28 October 2026, the Czech Constitutional Court publicly announces its decision on the opposition's request for an interim measure (předběžné opatření) against the law removing the president's power to appoint and recall heads of permanent missions.

Public means a press release or a decision posted on usoud.cz, a statement by the Court's spokesperson, or a report by ČTK, ČT24 or another major Czech outlet citing the Court. Granting the request, rejecting it, declaring it inadmissible, and a decision on the petition as a whole that disposes of the request all count. A decision taken in the window but first made public after 23:59 on 28 Oct does not count. These do not count: news that a judge-rapporteur has been assigned, that the Court is dealing with the request, or that it will decide later. NO if no decision is made public in the window, including if the Court does not decide the request separately before 1 Nov.
